issues.description: StockIngredient getter name mismatch: the template declares public String getIngredientName(), while the solution declares public String getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify exact getter names, creating an identifier-naming inconsistency. This mismatch also appears in Stock.findStockIngredient usages: the template's Stock.findStockIngredient calls getIngredientName(), while the solution's Stock.findStockIngredient calls getName(). This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected API and lead to compilation or test failures if other code or tests expect the alternative name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent across artifacts. Prefer using getName(): rename the template method getIngredientName() to getName() and update all template usages (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to call getName(). Alternatively, if you prefer getIngredientName(), rename the solution method and update solution usages. Ensure the problem statement/guidelines mention the chosen getter name if tests depend on it.

issues.description: StockIngredient.name getter naming is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" (does not mandate a specific getter name). The template repository implements the getter as StockIngredient.getIngredientName() and the template Stock.findStockIngredient() calls x.getIngredientName(). The solution repository implements the getter as StockIngredient.getName() and its Stock.findStockIngredient() calls x.getName(). This mismatch means students following the template or instructions may implement or rely on a different getter name than the solution/tests expect, causing confusion or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the StockIngredient.name field across all artifacts. Prefer getName() to match common Java conventions and align with Meal.getName(): - In the template repository, rename getIngredientName() to getName() and update any calls (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName(). - In the problem statement, either avoid specifying a getter name (keep the instruction generic: "add getters for all private fields") or explicitly state the chosen getter name (getName). - Ensure tests and solution use the same getter (getName) so students implementing according to the template or instructions are not blocked by naming differences.
